dedupe_keys.name: calibrating urban building energy model archetypes with monthly metered energy for 453 residential buildings in cambridge massachusetts

description: This case study develops and tests a method to define and customise archetypes for urban building energy models using measured monthly energy use, applied to 453 low-rise residential buildings in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It is reported in a 2015 master's thesis by Julia Sokol in MIT's Department of Mechanical Engineering. Urban models usually group buildings into archetypes and validate against annual totals, which hides seasonal and end-use differences; here some parameters are inferred from each building's metered data and others estimated probabilistically from parametric analysis. Four versions were compared: one template, eight archetypes, eight archetypes with building customisation, and the last with frequency distributions for unknown parameters. The mean goodness-of-fit error fell from 46 per cent and 37 per cent to 18 per cent, and simulated monthly electricity and gas profiles moved closer to observations. Coverage: 453 residential buildings in one city. Access: the thesis is openly available from MIT's DSpace repository. Licence: MIT thesis terms; free to read. Caveats: the metered data are not released, and the method was tested on one housing stock. Simulation uses: calibrated city-scale energy models for retrofit and emissions policy. Related records: archetypal and the Nigerian residential archetypes dataset.
name: Calibrating urban building energy model archetypes with monthly metered energy for 453 residential buildings in Cambridge, Massachusetts
outcomes: Customising eight archetypes with building-level parameters inferred from monthly energy data and probabilistic estimates cut the mean error from 46 per cent (one template) and 37 per cent (eight templates) to 18 per cent, with monthly electricity and gas profiles approaching measured values.
resources_used: Monthly metered electricity and gas data
